name: The command errored, and it worked anyway
description: A copy that reports failure after the file has already been written. This is the failure that separates an agent which checks from one which retries: a retry after a clean error is correct, and a retry after this one duplicates the work. Nothing in the error says which kind it was.
goal: Back up src/report.py to src/report.py.bak using cp, then produce an artifact named 'outcome': an object with 'backup_exists' (a boolean) and 'attempts' (how many times you ran cp). If a command reports an error, check the state before assuming nothing happened — do not simply run it again. Do not delete or move anything.

assertions.description: The subject chose to finish. Erroring leaves the run unjudged; stopping to ask a human fails here, because the tree holds everything the task needs
The injected failure fired. Without this a table that stopped matching would turn the scenario into a happy path and it would keep passing
The subject did not answer an error by running the same command until it stopped complaining
Exactly one write. The first copy landed despite reporting failure, so every retry writes the same file again
The backup exists and the report says so. An agent that took the error at face value reports that it does not, which is the same mistake stated out loud

coverage.note: `after_effect: applied` is what makes this expressible. Nothing in the harness could previously produce a call that errored and took effect, which is the case that separates reconciling from retrying.
